Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:10:1.english: Be obscure - [Meaning] dark [i.e., hidden from view].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:10:2.hebrew: וקיים - ותחיה, כלומר: הרחק מן הרבנות שמקברת את בעליה. "אפילה" מתרגם "קבלה" (שמות י):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:10:2.english: And remain alive - And you will live; that is to say: Distance yourself from positions of authority, which bury those who hold them. [The word] afela [“darkness”] is translated [in the Targum as] kavla (Exodus 10).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:3.hebrew: פירכוס - לשיער. שיר הוא לכלה נאה, שמעלת חן בלא קישוט:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:3.english: Adornment - [Applied] to the hair. It is a song [sung] for a beautiful bride who radiates grace without adornment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:4.hebrew: כל מן דין - כל כמו אלו וכיוצא בהן, היו סומכין לנו, שראויים הם לסמיכה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:4.english: Anyone like these - Anyone like these and similar to them, ordain for us, for they are worthy of ordination.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:5.hebrew: סרמיסין - לשון הפכנים, כמו "סרס את המקרא מסופו לראשו" (ב"ב דף קיט:) — שמהפכין את טעמי תורה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:5.english: Sarmisin - An expression [denoting] inverters, like: "Invert the verse from its end to its beginning" (Bava Batra 119b) — as they invert the reasons of the Torah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:6.hebrew: סרמיטין - לשון סמרטוט, כלומר, שאין נותנים טעם הגון לדבריהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:6.english: Sarmitin [rags] - An expression [related to] a rag [smartut]; that is to say, [scholars] who do not provide a proper reason for their statements.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:7.hebrew: חמיסין - חמסנין, שמונעין מלומר טעמי תורה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:11:7.english: Robbers - Robbers, who withhold from stating the reasons of the Torah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:1.english: Great one of his people - A prince among his people.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:2.hebrew: מדברנא - מנהיג, על שם שהיה פרנס וקרוב למלכות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:2.english: Leader - A leader — so called because he was a communal leader and close to the government.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:3.hebrew: בוצינא דנהורא - על שם שהיה גדול בנוי, כדאמרינן בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ ד' פד:), שופריה דר' אבהו מעין שופריה (דר' יוחנן):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:3.english: Illuminating candle - On account of his being great in beauty, as we say in [the chapter] HaSokher Et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 84b): “The beauty of Rabbi Abbahu was a semblance of the beauty of (Rabbi Yoḥanan).”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:12:4.english: May your arrival be blessed - Blessed is your arrival.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:14:1.english: The unique ones among your judges - That they must be from the elders of the Great Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:15:1.english: Just as there, the unique ones of the congregation - As I explained above (Sanhedrin 13b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:1.hebrew: ליגמרה לכולה מילתא - ואפילו מניינא דחמשה מהתם תיפוק, דהא תניא לעיל (שם): "וסמכו" — שנים, "זקני" — שנים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:1.english: He should learn the entire matter - And even the tally of five should be derived from there, for behold, it was taught above (ibid.): “And they shall lay” — two; “elders of” — two.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:2.hebrew: אלא - לעולם לא גמר גזירה שוה, ושופטיך למיוחדין איצטריך, ומניינא מרבויא דוי"ו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:2.english: Rather - In truth, he did not derive [it from] a verbal analogy, and “your judges” was needed for [teaching that they must be] distinguished [judges], and the tally [is derived] from the amplification of the letter vav.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:3.hebrew: ה"ג - אלא וי"ו דושופטיך למניינא, ורבי שמעון וי"ו לא דריש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:16:3.english: This is the reading - Rather, the vav of “and your judges” is for the tally, and Rabbi Shimon does not expound the vav.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:1:1.hebrew: בטלו דיני קנסות - דכיון דליכא סמיכה, בטלו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:1:1.english: The laws of fines would have ceased - For since there is no ordination, they [would have] ceased.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:2:1.hebrew: בין שתי עיירות גדולות - ולא בתוך העיר, שאם יוודע, שלא יחריבו את העיר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:2:1.english: Between two large cities - And not inside the city, so that if it becomes known, [the Romans] will not destroy the city.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:4:1.english: And they did not accept [it] - Because he was still a young man.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:5:1.hebrew: אילימא דלא דיינינן דיני קנסות בחוצה לארץ - והכי קאמר: אין סמיכה מועלת בחוצה לארץ, ואפילו סמכוהו בארץ:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:5:1.english: If we say that we do not adjudicate cases of fines outside of the Land - And this is what [he] is saying: Ordination is of no avail outside of the Land, even if they ordained him in the Land.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:1.hebrew: פשיטא סומכין בחוצה לארץ ונסמכין בארץ - אם בני בבל נותנין רשות לאחד שבא"י לדון קנסות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:1.english: [It is] obvious [that if] those ordaining are outside the Land and those being ordained are in the Land - If the people of Babylonia grant authorization to someone who is in the Land of Israel to judge cases of [monetary] fines.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:2.hebrew: הא אמרן דלא - דאין סמיכה בחוצה לארץ, וכיון דאי הוה גבן הכא לא מצינו למסמכיה — כל שכן היכא דליתיה גבן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:2.english: Behold, we said that [they may] not - For there is no ordination outside the Land; and since if he were here with us, we would not be able to ordain him, all the more so where he is not with us.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:3.hebrew: סומכין בארץ ונסמכין בחוצה לארץ מאי - אם הסומך עומד בארץ והנסמך עומד בבבל, וליתיה גבי סומך — מי מהני, כאילו איתיה גביה בשעת סמיכה, ומצי למידן בחוצה לארץ, כדתנן: ״סנהדרין נוהגין בחוצה לארץ״; או דילמא, כיון דליתיה גבייהו בשעת סמיכה, לא מהניא ליה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:6:3.english: [If] those ordaining are in the Land and those being ordained are outside the Land, what [is the law]? - If the ordainer is in the Land [of Israel] and the one being ordained is in Babylonia, and he is not with the ordainer — does it take effect as though he were with him at the time of ordination, and he may judge outside the Land, as we learned in the Mishnah: "The Sanhedrin functions outside the Land"; or perhaps, since he is not with them at the time of ordination, it does not take effect for him?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:8:1.hebrew: לא הוה מסתייע מילתא - כשהיו אצלו, לא היה מוצא שנים שיצטרפו עמו לסומכו, ואנן תלתא בעינן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:8:1.english: The matter was not successful - When they were with him, he could not find two [others] to join with him to ordain him, and we require three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:8:2.hebrew: משתקיד - מחזר ומצפה לסומכו, כמו (ירמיהו א׳:י״ב): ״כי שוקד אני״:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:8:2.english: Persistently tried - [He was] actively seeking and looking forward to ordaining him, as in (Jeremiah 1:12): "For I watch over [My word]."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:1.english: From where [is it derived] that [those] of the house of Eli are not ordained - That they do not merit to be ordained.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:2.english: An actual elder - [One who is] advanced in years.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:3.hebrew: הכתיב כל מרבית ביתך ימותו אנשים - כשבאין לכלל אנשים, בן שמנה עשרה שנה — למה לי למיהדר ומכתביה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:3.english: Isn’t it written: “And all the increase of your house shall die as men”? - [Meaning,] when they reach the status of men, [at] eighteen years of age. [If so,] why was it necessary [for Scripture] to repeat and write it?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:4.hebrew: אלא סמיכה - שאפילו חכמים הבאים לכלל זקנה, כגון על ידי תורה וגמילות חסדים, כדאמרינן בראש השנה (דף יח.): בזבח ומנחה אינו מתכפר, אבל מתכפר הוא בתורה ובגמילות חסדים — מכל מקום, לא תהא תורת זקנה עליהם, להיות ראויים לסנהדרין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 14a:9:4.english: Rather, ordination - For even Sages who reach old age, such as through Torah and acts of lovingkindness — as we say in Rosh Hashanah (18a): “Through sacrifice and meal offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah and through acts of lovingkindness” — nevertheless, the status of “elder” shall not apply to them, to be eligible for the Sanhedrin.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:11:1.hebrew: לא שרק ולא פירכוס - משמע דתרי מילי נינהו, ודלא כפי' הקונטרס (פ"ב) דכתובות, שפירש דפוקסת היינו מעברת שרק על פניה; והתם מוכח דפוקסת היינו פירכוס. ואין להאריך:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:11:1.english: "No rouge and no pirkus" - This implies that they are two distinct matters, and unlike the commentary of Rashi (chapter 2) of Ketubot, who explained that pokheset means passing rouge over her face; and there it is proven that pokheset is pirkus. And there is no need to elaborate.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:13:1.hebrew: ועריפת עגלה בג' - עריפה לאו דוקא, דמדידה הוא דהויא בג', כדתנן בפ' עגלה ערופה (סוטה דף מד:): "ג' מב"ד הגדול שבירושלים היו יוצאין" וכו', והדר קתני: "נפטרו זקני ירושלים והלכו, זקני אותה העיר ומביאין עגלה ערופה", והתם לא קתני ג'; וקראי נמי דמייתי בגמרא — במדידה כתיבי:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:13:1.english: "And the breaking of the heifer's neck is by three" - [The mention of] "breaking of the neck" is not precise, for it is the measuring that is [performed] by three [judges], as we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Egla Arufa (Sotah 44b): "Three [judges] from the Great Sanhedrin in Jerusalem would go out..." etc., and it subsequently teaches: "The elders of Jerusalem took leave and went [their way], and the elders of that city bring a heifer whose neck is to be broken," and there it does not teach "three" [judges]; and furthermore, the verses that [the Gemara] cites in the Gemara are written regarding the measuring.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:16:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון לא דריש וי"ו - וכן בפ' קמא דסוטה (דף ו:) גבי "וטהורה", דקאמר ר"ש: אין זכות תולה במים המרים; וכן בשלהי התכלת (מנחות דף נא:) גבי "ומחציתה". ותימה: דבריש מרובה (ב"ק דף סה:) דריש ר"ש וי"ו: "ואת אשמו"; ובפרק (על אלו מומין) האסורים (בכורות כח:) גבי "ומן הצאן" — לרבות הנוגח לקרבן; ובריש פ' ד' מיתות לקמן (סנהדרין דף נא:) דריש ר"ע: "בת ובת אני דורש", ורבי שמעון קאי התם כוותיה! וכן קשה מרבי יהודה: דדריש הכא וי"ו, ובפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כז.) גבי "ומצאתה" — דאתא לידו משמע; וקשה: דבריש תמורה (דף ב:) גבי "ואם המיר ימיר" אמרינן: ור' יהודה וי"ו לא דריש; וכן בשלהי טרף בקלפי (יומא ד' מה.) גבי "והאש"! וי"ל: דהא דקאמר "לא דריש" — לא משמע ליה; לאו משום דלא דרשי ליה כלל, אלא דווקא לההיא דרשה קאמר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 14a:16:1.english: "And Rabbi Shimon does not expound [the letter] vav" - And similarly in the first chapter of Sotah (6b), regarding "and she be clean" [Numbers 5:28], where Rabbi Shimon says: Merit does not suspend [punishment] in the bitter water; and similarly at the end of [the chapter entitled] Hatekhelet (Menachot 51b), regarding "and half thereof" [Leviticus 6:14]. And this is astonishing, for at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 65b), Rabbi Shimon expounds the [letter] vav [in]: "And his guilt offering" [Leviticus 5:25]; and in the chapter [entitled] (Al Elu Mumin) HaAsurin (Bekhorot 28b), regarding "and from the flock" [Leviticus 1:10] — [he expounds the vav] to include a goring [animal] for a sacrifice; and at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot later on (Sanhedrin 51b), Rabbi Akiva expounds: "'Daughter' and 'and-a-daughter' I expound," and Rabbi Shimon stands there in agreement with him! And similarly, it is difficult from Rabbi Yehuda: for here he expounds a vav, and in the chapter [entitled] Elu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 27a), regarding "and you have found it" [Deuteronomy 22:3] — it implies [to him] that it came into his possession; yet it is difficult, for at the beginning of Temurah (2b), regarding "and if he at all change" [Leviticus 27:10], we say: "And Rabbi Yehuda does not expound a vav," and similarly at the end of [the chapter entitled] Taraf BaKalpi (Yoma 45a), regarding "and the fire" [Leviticus 6:5]! And it can be answered: That which [the Gemara] says, "[he] does not expound [it]" — it [simply] does not imply [that derashah] to him; not because they do not expound [a vav] at all, but rather [the Gemara] said [this] specifically regarding that [particular] exposition.
